$comment: RCS-1/2/4 as a verification step (the recourse family, TRM-9). RCS-1: every consequential transaction MUST carry a forum designation, recorded INSIDE the terms record — so the elections are read from the hashed ATR bytes themselves, never from a caller-supplied side channel; what is proved is what was welded. RCS-2: governing law MUST be elected and recorded. RCS-4: the transaction MUST produce a self-contained evidence package — the required roles are the specification's own enumeration (terms artifact; acceptance signature and its authority chain; the spend-authorization artifact or a verifiable reference; identity attestations and their assurance; the settlement reference and weld; timestamps), minus its explicitly conditional clause (fulfillment/order-state, 'where performance is disputed'). This step NEVER returns failed: an absent election is absence of proof, not a contradiction in the record, and must not impeach supportedClass to TC-0. Authored from the specification before the implementation existed. 2026-09-02: every record here now opens with "atrVersion":"0.3". The ATR's format-version member was `lcp`, which collided with the LCP specification's own version line, and then briefly `atr`, which named the artifact rather than its version; a version field names what it versions. No case in this area pins a hash, so no digest moved.
